articles.headline: Understanding the UK's Minimum Wage System
articles.excerpt: The UK operates a system of minimum wage rates, including the National Living Wage and National Minimum Wage, to ensure fair pay for workers.

Beginner.text:
In the UK, there is a special rule about how much money workers must get paid. It's called the minimum wage. This means employers cannot pay less than this amount.
There are two main types of minimum wage. One is the National Living Wage (NLW). This is for people who are 23 years old or older. The other is the National Minimum Wage (NMW). This is for younger workers, like those aged 22 and under.
From April 2024, if you are 23 or older, the National Living Wage is £11.44 for every hour you work. If you are 21 or 22, the National Minimum Wage is £8.60 per hour. For people aged 18 to 20, it is £6.40 per hour. And for workers under 18, it is £5.44 per hour.
These amounts change every year. The government looks at the economy and decides new rates. This usually happens in April. The idea is to make sure people earn enough money to live. It helps many workers across the country get fair pay.

The United Kingdom operates a system of legally mandated minimum pay rates, ensuring that all eligible workers receive a fair baseline income. This system is primarily divided into two categories: the National Living Wage (NLW) and the National Minimum Wage (NMW). These rates are updated annually by the government, typically taking effect each April.
The National Living Wage applies to workers aged 23 and over. As of April 2024, the NLW is set at £11.44 per hour. This rate aims to reflect a wage level that helps cover the basic cost of living for older workers.
For younger workers, the National Minimum Wage applies. There are different rates depending on age. Workers aged 21 to 22 are entitled to £8.60 per hour. Those aged 18 to 20 receive £6.40 per hour, and workers under 18 are paid £5.44 per hour. Apprentices also have a specific minimum rate, which is £6.40 per hour, regardless of their age, if they are under 19 or in the first year of their apprenticeship.
The purpose of these minimum wage laws is to protect low-paid workers, reduce poverty, and ensure a basic standard of living. The annual review process considers economic conditions and recommendations from independent bodies to determine appropriate increases, aiming to balance the needs of employees with the capacity of businesses. The National Minimum Wage was initially introduced in the UK in 1999, marking a significant policy shift towards addressing in-work poverty and ensuring fair remuneration. Beginner.text:
Nvidia is a big technology company. It makes special computer parts called GPUs. These parts are very important for video games and new computer intelligence, like AI.

When people talk about "stock," they mean small pieces of a company that you can buy. If the company does well, the stock price might go up.

The year has four parts, called quarters. The fourth quarter is October, November, and December. News shows that Nvidia's stock often goes up in these months. This has happened many times. In fact, in 20 of the last 27 years, Nvidia's stock has risen during the fourth quarter.

Why does this happen? Maybe because people buy more electronics for holidays like Christmas, and Nvidia's parts are in many of these products. Or maybe investors feel more hopeful at the end of the year.

It's important to remember that what happened in the past might not happen again. The stock market can change. But for Nvidia, the fourth quarter has often been a good time for its stock.
